RelativeFarguesFontaine.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is in the libraries. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has perfectoid spaces, diamonds, v-sheaves or any Fargues-Fontaine curve, and ramified Witt vectors W_{O_E} do not exist at all; Mathlib's Witt theory is p-typical only. What does exist and is genuinely usable is upstream infrastructure: Mathlib's `WittVector` with Frobenius, Teichmuller lifts, p-adic completeness and the W(k)-is-a-DVR theorem; Fontaine's theta with surjectivity; and an absolute `BDeRhamPlus`/`BDeRham` for a single p-adically complete ring (with principality of ker theta, the theta-extension and the DVR property all still open TODOs in that file). On the geometric side Tau Ceti supplies the entire Huber-ring and adic-spectrum layer RF0 presupposes — Huber pairs, Spa(A,A+) with spectrality, rational subsets and their basis/refinement calculus, completed rational localisation A<T/s> with its integrally closed plus ring, and the identification of Spa of that pair with the rational subset — all sorry-free. Genuinely missing is everything the roadmap names: the ramified Witt algebra and its universal property, 𝒴_S and Y_S, the perfectoidness of the charts and their tilt, sheafiness, the phi-quotient X_S, Div^d and B_D, relative B_dR, O(n) and the graded algebra, and Beauville-Laszlo patching in both its linear and Tannakian forms.

targets.target: Ramified Witt vectors W_{O_E}(R) for a perfect F_q-algebra R and a nonarchimedean local coefficient field E
targets.note: Mathlib has only the p-typical `WittVector p R`, i.e. the case E = Q_p, O_E = Z_p, q = p. There is no O_E-coefficient (ramified) Witt construction anywhere: `grep -rn -i 'ramified witt\|W_\{O_E\}'` over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Teichmuller representatives in W_{O_E}(R)
targets.note: `WittVector.teichmuller` is the multiplicative monoid hom R ->* W(R) in the p-typical case only; the O_E-version is absent.

targets.target: Frobenius on W_{O_E}(R) (the q-Frobenius)
targets.note: Mathlib's `WittVector.frobenius` is the p-power Witt Frobenius; `frobeniusEquiv` makes it an isomorphism for a perfect base. The q = p^f Frobenius of a ramified coefficient ring is not constructed.

targets.target: pi-adically complete flat O_E universal property of W_{O_E}
targets.note: Mathlib proves p-adic completeness of W(R) for a perfect ring (`isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP`) and a universal property only as the inverse limit of truncated Witt vectors (`WittVector.lift`). The strict-lift universal property (unique pi-adically complete flat O_E-algebra with W/pi = R) is not stated, in either the p-typical or the ramified case.

targets.target: Mixed-characteristic comparison with the completed scalar extension of W(-) over W(F_q)
targets.note: No comparison W_{O_E}(R) = W(R) ⊗_{W(F_q)} O_E (completed) exists; `WittVector/Compare.lean` only compares W(ZMod p) with Z_p.

targets.target: Equal-characteristic identification W_{O_E}(R) = R[[pi]]
targets.note: `PowerSeries R` exists in Mathlib but there is no Witt-vector identification with it; the equal-characteristic case of ramified Witt vectors is not formalised.

targets.target: Functoriality, reduction, topology and uniformizer-change comparisons
targets.note: `WittVector.map` gives functoriality and `WittVector.Complete` gives the p-adic topology, both p-typically. Uniformizer-change comparison has no counterpart because there is no uniformizer parameter.

duplicates.note: Layer 6.1 of the AdicSpaces roadmap packages W(O_F), Frobenius and Teichmuller lifts with the (p,[varpi])-adic topology; RF0 is the same package for a general coefficient field E.
F0 explicitly imports A_inf = W(O_F) and its (p,[varpi])-adic topology from AdicSpaces Layer 6 rather than rebuilding it; RF0 is the ramified generalisation of exactly that object.

GS0:Witt-geometry says outright it will 'reuse RF0's ramified Witt algebra rather than a second coefficient ring'.

targets.target: W_{O_E}(R^+) with the (pi,[varpi])-adic topology as a Huber ring
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the full Huber-ring/pair-of-definition API and Mathlib has W(R) with p-adic completeness, but nobody assembles W(O_F) (let alone W_{O_E}(R^+)) into a Huber ring with the (pi,[varpi])-adic topology; the AdicSpaces roadmap itself lists this as unbuilt Layer 6 work.

targets.target: The integral period space 𝒴_S = Spa(W_{O_E}(R^+)) \ V([varpi]) over Spa(O_E)
targets.note: Tau Ceti's `spa` and its spectrality exist for an arbitrary Huber pair, but no instance is formed for a Witt ring and 𝒴 is nowhere defined. Neither library has any perfectoid space, diamond or v-sheaf: the whole Scholze-style carrier is absent (Mathlib's `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/` is only FontaineTheta, Untilt and BDeRham, and there is no `IsPerfectoid` predicate).

targets.target: The rational cover |pi|^n <= |[varpi]| != 0 of 𝒴_S
targets.note: The general theory of rational subsets and their basis property is complete in Tau Ceti; the specific annular windows of the period space are not constructed.

targets.target: Completed rational chart rings with integral-closure plus rings
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds A<T/s> as the separated completion of the topological localisation, defines its plus ring as the integral closure of the image of A^+ adjoined the fractions, proves it is a ring of integral elements, and identifies Spa of the pair with the rational subset. This is exactly the general construction the layer needs, but it is never applied to the Witt chart rings and nothing perfectoid is proved about them.

targets.target: FS II.1.1: after O_E -> O_{E_infty} the charts are perfectoid and their tilt glues to the perfected open unit disc over S
targets.note: There is no perfectoid ring predicate and no tilting equivalence; `PreTilt` is the inverse-limit perfection of R/p and carries none of this.

targets.target: Sheafiness of the charts by the topological direct-summand argument
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the reduction of the sheaf condition to rational covers but no sheafiness theorem at all (neither the strongly noetherian nor the stably uniform one), so no direct-summand argument can be run.

TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic.summary: Nothing in this roadmap exists in either library, and the gap is unusually clean: 'Berkovich', 'tropicalization' in the geometric sense, 'balancing', 'Baker-Norine', 'Mumford', 'Schottky', 'Tate curve', 'Coleman integration' and 'metrized line bundle' all return zero hits across Mathlib and Tau Ceti. Mathlib's `Tropical` is only the min-plus semiring. What is available is adjacent infrastructure of real use: Tau Ceti's complete adic-spectrum layer (Spa(A,A+) with arbitrary-rank valuative points, rational subsets, analytic points, residue-field valuations, the closed polydisc with its classical points), its models of curves over a DVR with finite DVR extensions, its numerical types (the weighted dual graph with vertex genera, the arithmetic-genus formula, and Pic(T) = coker of the weighted intersection matrix, proved of rank one with finite torsion — the combinatorial Jacobian TB.3 wants), its PL/convex-polyhedron and toric-cone machinery, and the full function-field Riemann-Roch theorem. Genuinely missing is every stage's own content: the Berkovich spectrum and its comparison with Spa, the point-type classification and the skeleton metric, analytification and retraction, the graph Laplacian/specialization/slope formula and Baker-Norine, tropicalization with weights and balancing, faithful tropicalization, model metrics and measures, local heights, and Tate/Mumford uniformization with its integration interfaces.

targets.target: The Berkovich spectrum M(A) of a Banach algebra as the set of bounded multiplicative seminorms
targets.note: The word 'Berkovich' does not occur in either library: `grep -rn -i berkovich` over Mathlib and Tau Ceti returns nothing. Mathlib has the bundled `MulRingSeminorm`/`RingSeminorm` that would be its points, and `WeakDual.characterSpace` is the archimedean Gelfand analogue (continuous unital algebra homs with the weak-* topology), but no nonarchimedean spectrum is formed from them.

targets.note: Only the character space of a topological algebra carries a weak-* topology in Mathlib; there is no seminorm-valued analogue.

targets.note: Tau Ceti builds the residue ring and the induced valuation on the residue field of a point of Spa (`residueFieldValuation`), which is the adic counterpart; the Berkovich completed residue field H(x) is absent. Mathlib's `spectralNorm` is the norm on an algebraic extension of a nonarchimedean field, a different object.

targets.note: Tau Ceti has models of a curve over a DVR: a flat, finitely presented total space with a chosen identification of the generic fibre, properness as a separate predicate, and the category of finite DVR extensions the semistable-reduction theorem produces. targets.note: `TauCeti.NumericalType` is exactly the dual graph datum — components with multiplicities, weights, genera and a symmetric intersection matrix whose adjacency relation is required connected (Stacks 0C6Z). VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals.summary: The one real library asset is Mathlib's `WittVector.Isocrystal`: a K(p,k)-vector space with a Frobenius-semilinear automorphism, with morphisms, isomorphisms, the standard slope-m object and the Dieudonné-Manin classification proved in dimension one over an algebraically closed field. That is VB0's category and the r = 1 case of its classification, for the coefficient field E = Q_p only - substantial, but no VB0 target is met in the stated generality, so the stage is ranked not built rather than partly built. Tau Ceti adds a Brauer group of central simple algebras with base change and splitting, but no cyclic algebra and no local invariant Br(E) = Q/Z, so VB0's Brauer-invariant obligation stands. Everything else in the roadmap is missing at the level of its carrier: there is no Fargues-Fontaine curve, no perfectoid space, no diamond or v-sheaf, and - strikingly - no semistability or Harder-Narasimhan formalism anywhere in either library, in any setting, so VB1's slope theory, VB2's classification, VB3's Banach-Colmez spaces and VB4's relative HN strata have neither objects nor the general machinery they would specialise.

targets.target: Finite-dimensional spaces over E-breve with a bijective sigma-semilinear operator, their morphisms, and the category of isocrystals
targets.note: Mathlib does have isocrystals: a K(p,k)-vector space with a φ-semilinear automorphism, over the fraction field of W(k) for a perfect integral domain k of characteristic p, together with homomorphisms and isomorphisms. Two things the stage asks for are missing: the coefficient field is E = ℚ_p only (there is no q-Frobenius over a ramified E-breve), and the class carries no finiteness hypothesis, so `finrank = 1` or `Module.Finite` must be added by hand.

targets.target: Exact tensor category structure on isocrystals and descent
targets.note: Mathlib's `Isocrystal` is a bare class; there is no `Category`, no monoidal/tensor structure, no exactness and no descent statement. Nothing in Tau Ceti adds any of this.

targets.target: The Dieudonné–Manin classification over an algebraically closed residue base: simple objects of rational slope, multiplicities, Hom spaces and endomorphism division algebras
targets.note: Mathlib proves the classification only in dimension one: over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, a one-dimensional isocrystal is isomorphic to the standard slope-m object for some m : ℤ. The general finite-dimensional statement, the simple objects of rational (non-integral) slope, the multiplicities, and the Hom and endomorphism division algebras are absent — `grep -rn -i 'dieudonn|isocrystal'` finds nothing beyond this one file.

targets.target: The Brauer invariant of the endomorphism algebra and its compatibility with the explicit cyclic algebra
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a Brauer group of central simple algebras with base change, splitting fields and the group law, and an abstract class-formation invariant-map normalisation in `TauCeti/Algebra/AddCircle.lean`. What the stage needs is not there: no cyclic (crossed-product) algebra construction and no local invariant Br(E) ≅ ℚ/ℤ (`grep -rn -i 'cyclic algebra|crossed product|Hasse invariant'` over both libraries returns nothing), so the invariant cannot be computed.

targets.target: The standard rank-r isocrystal with Frobenius r-th power π^s σ^r, the slope of its associated bundle, and the sign convention
targets.note: Only r = 1, s = m: the standard object has Φ(x) = p^m · φ(x). There is no rank-r block, and no associated bundle to take the slope of, since the Fargues–Fontaine curve does not exist in either library.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces.summary: This is by some distance the most-built roadmap in the batch: Tau Ceti carries a ~28000-line, sorry-free development under `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/` and `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/` that covers Layers 0-2 almost completely. Layer 1 is finished - Spv A with its patch presentation and spectrality, the pro-constructible calculus, cofinal ideals and c-Gamma_v(I), Spv(A,I) with the retraction r_I and Lemma 7.5, Cont A with Theorem 7.10 and Corollary 7.12 - and Layer 0 and Layer 2 are complete apart from named gaps. What is genuinely missing, in order: Weierstrass division/preparation and the noetherianity of K<X_1,...,X_n>, so that BGR 5.2.6 is unproved and no nondiscrete ring is yet known to be strongly noetherian; the family-indexed topological localisation A(T/S) (only the singleton-denominator case exists); Wedhorn 6.9(1); Proposition 8.2(2) in full and Definition 7.56's affinoid algebras; the homeomorphism Spa(A_U,A_U+) = U for the *completed* localisation, which the library states as an open problem; the structure sheaf O_X itself, O_X+, stalks, the category V^pre and the three sheafiness predicates; Lemmas 8.33/8.34, the Cech statement, stable uniformity and Buzzard-Verberkmoes; the whole of Layer 5's adic-space geometry and gluing; and all of Layer 6 except Mathlib's Witt-vector package. The Layer 4 *algebra* - Remark 8.29, Lemma 8.31, Proposition 8.30 in full and Corollary 8.32 - is done, so Tate acyclicity is blocked only on its last two lemmas and on a sheafiness predicate to state the conclusion in.

targets.target: Bounded subsets of a topological ring and their elementary calculus (subsets, finite unions, products, finite sets, images, transport along topological ring isomorphisms)
targets.note: Bounded.lean states the definition exactly as in mathlib4#40013 (the PR the layer asks to coordinate with) and proves subsets, unions, finite sets, finite pointwise products, images and transport. Boundedness is not preserved by an arbitrary continuous map, and the file carries the extra open-at-zero hypothesis the layer asks to be stated separately.

targets.note: Mathlib's `SpectralSpace` extends `CompactSpace` (Mathlib/Topology/Spectral/Basic.lean:38), so the `SpectralSpace (spa Aplus)` instance at Spa/Spectral.lean:90 gives quasi-compactness of Spa(A,A⁺) immediately, and for an arbitrary subring as plus ring.

duplicates.note: R0 states the same open and closed immersions and the same presentation-independence obligation, adding separatedness, finite, smooth and étale maps; the two stages own the same open/closed-immersion construction, this one without fibre products.
A1 defines étale morphisms by a local open-immersion/finite-étale description, so it needs and restates this layer's open immersions of analytic adic spaces.
D6 glues the affine objects Spd(A,A⁺) to define X^♢ for analytic adic spaces, which presupposes this layer's gluing of adic spaces as its input.

targets.target: Witt vectors W(𝒪_F) of a perfect characteristic-p ring, their Frobenius, and Teichmüller lifts
targets.note: This is the one package in the layer the libraries supply outright: W(R) for any commutative ring, the Witt Frobenius (an isomorphism for a perfect base), the multiplicative Teichmüller lift, and p-adic completeness of W(R) for perfect R. Mathlib also has the perfection/tilt (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean`) and Fontaine's θ.

targets.target: A_inf = W(𝒪_F) as a complete Hausdorff Huber ring with pair of definition (A_inf,(p,[ϖ])) and plus ring A_inf, and the proof that it has no topologically nilpotent unit, hence is not Tate
targets.note: No A_inf exists in either library: `grep -rn -i 'A_inf'` over TauCeti returns one unrelated hit and every `Ainf` hit is an A-infinity algebra. The (p,[ϖ])-adic topology, its completeness and separatedness, and the non-Tate statement are all unformalised; only the general Huber vocabulary and the analogous ℤ_p example exist.

targets.target: 𝒴 = {v ∈ Spa(A_inf,A_inf) : v(p[ϖ]) ≠ 0} = D(p) ∩ D([ϖ]): open, nonempty, Frobenius-stable, with an explicit Gauss point, and the identification of the analytic locus as D(p) ∪ D([ϖ])
targets.note: The generic analytic-locus theory the layer cites is built (Layer 2), but 𝒴 itself, its Frobenius stability and the Gauss point are not; there is no Gauss point for the Witt ring (`MvPowerSeries.gaussNorm` is the unrelated coefficientwise Gauss norm).

targets.target: Power comparability of v(p) and v([ϖ]) on 𝒴, the order-theoretic radius κ(v), and κ(φ(v)) = p·κ(v)
targets.note: Nothing: no radius function, no Frobenius action on valuations of a Witt ring.

targets.target: Kedlaya windows U_n, V_n at breakpoint c = (p+1)/2: rational subsets covering 𝒴, Frobenius index shift, disjointness of translates, freeness of the ℤ-action and wanderingness
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'wandering|kedlaya'` over both libraries returns nothing.

targets.target: The quotient space 𝒳 = 𝒴/φ^ℤ: open quotient map, injectivity on each wandering window, the U_0/V_0 image cover, quasi-compactness and T0
targets.note: Absent; no Fargues–Fontaine object of any kind exists (`grep -rn -i fargues` over both libraries: zero hits).

targets.target: Kedlaya's interval rings B^I for I = [s,r] ⊂ (0,∞) with the norm λ_I: complete Hausdorff Tate, strongly noetherian (Kedlaya Theorem 4.10), unit ball equal to the power-bounded subring and a ring of integral elements, comparison with the localised A_inf plus ring, and the reciprocal-radius dictionary between window and interval parameters
targets.note: No interval ring exists. The strong-noetherianness predicate it would have to satisfy is defined, but no nondiscrete ring is proved to satisfy it anywhere in the library, so even the target of Kedlaya 4.10 has no instance to land in.

targets.target: The quotient sheaf 𝒪_𝒳(U) = 𝒪_𝒴(q⁻¹U)^{φ=1} as a sheaf of complete separated topological rings, with stalk valuations independent of the orbit representative
targets.note: Absent; 𝒪_𝒴 itself does not exist, since the Layer 3 structure sheaf is not constructed.

targets.target: The five window-chart statements: q⁻¹(q(W)) is the disjoint union of translates; q|_W a homeomorphism onto q(W); W ≅ Spa(B^I,B^{I,+}) as affinoid pre-adic spaces; 𝒪_𝒳(q(V)) ≅ 𝒪_𝒴(V); naturality with plus rings and residue-field valuations, making 𝒳 an adic space
targets.note: Absent, and blocked upstream: it needs Layer 3.4's 𝒱^pre, Layer 4's sheafiness, and Layer 5's local-to-global assertion, none of which exist.

targets.target: Independence of the pseudouniformiser: (p,[ϖ]) and (p,[ϖ']) define the same topology, the two 𝒴 and their Frobenius actions are identified, and the quotient adic spaces are isomorphic
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: F0 explicitly imports this layer's outputs — A_inf = W(𝒪_F), Y_F = D(p) ∩ D([ϖ]), the quotient q : Y_F → X_F, the (p,[ϖ])-adic topology, the rational annuli, the Witt Frobenius, the wandering charts and the independence-of-ϖ isomorphisms — and restates them as its interface, so the two stages name the same objects.

RF0 builds the same period annuli and quotient over an arbitrary perfectoid base and an arbitrary coefficient field E, with ramified Witt vectors W_{O_E}; this layer is its E = ℚ_p, fixed-field special case.
RF0:integral-Y retains the integral period space before removing the special fibre, which is the relative counterpart of this layer's 𝒴 ⊂ Spa(A_inf,A_inf).
F1's untilt product formula uses the universal property of Witt vectors of the perfect ring 𝒪_F and Fontaine's θ, i.e. the same Witt-vector package this layer's 6.1 asks to be packaged.
